name: Sliding cabinet

evidence.source: Project-authored teaching example; no source-object or physical-test evidence

relations.label: Rail → drawer
relations.mechanism: A prismatic guide allows translation along one axis and limits transverse movement.
relations.conditions: The guides remain aligned, engaged and adequately supported.
relations.result: The drawer can move outward while remaining guided.
relations.intervention: Removing a guide may permit skewing or jamming. The outcome depends on the remaining supports.

relations.label: Side → top panel
relations.mechanism: The side panel provides one part of the load path beneath the top.
relations.conditions: The joints remain connected and the material can carry the applied load.
relations.result: Loads can pass from the top into the frame.
relations.intervention: Removing the side changes the load path; stability depends on the remaining connections.

reasoning_tasks.compose: Combine a shell, drawer and aligned guides to create accessible storage.
reasoning_tasks.decompose: One possible decomposition is a shell, drawer, guides and handle. Other storage mechanisms are possible.
reasoning_tasks.intervene: If a rail becomes misaligned, will the drawer still move freely? Identify the assumed clearance.
reasoning_tasks.transfer: Compare drawer guides with a sliding door: both constrain translation, with different support and load requirements.

limitations: Not an accepted dataset record, simulated outcome or measured model result.
